alt: Table declaring the ATUS 2024 release: universe, the diary-day weight, day-of-week sampling, the absence of design variables in the book's extract, the producer's 160 replicate weights, pooling, and known traps.
note: Provenance: design.json = machine-readable manifest field; design.json notes = the manifest's free text; producer = documentation read 2026-09-10; computed = counted from the store by build.py; book guidance = editorial, not a producer rule.

rows.value: Civilian noninstitutional population age 15 and older; one person per household, drawn from households completing their final CPS interview
diary-day weight: sums to person-DAYS, not persons (2003-2019, 2021+)
WT06 (BLS: TUFNWGTP on multi-year files, TUFINLWGT on annual files)
WT20: REQUIRED for any analysis touching 2020 (COVID collection break; represents Jan1-Mar17 + May10-Dec31 2020 only)
10 percent of the sample is assigned to each weekday and 25 percent to each weekend day; the weights return weekdays to about 5/7 of person-days

Weights only: no strata, PSUs, or replicate weights in the extract (STRATA is empty), so no design-based SE is possible. No replicate weights in store: weights-only variance understates SEs; BLS publishes replicate weights if needed later.

rows.source: producer: BLS ATUS user's guide; IPUMS ATUS
rows.value: 160 replicate final weights (IPUMS RWT06_1–RWT06_160; BLS FINLWGT001–FINLWGT160); Var = (4/160) × Σ_r (Ŷ_r − Ŷ_0)², the 4 coming from replicate factors 1.7, 1.0, and 0.3
Not stated by BLS; the replicate-count convention gives 159
Combine years whose weights were built the same way: WT06 for 2003–2019 and 2021 onward, WT20 for 2020. Do NOT splice WT06/WT20 into one column.
2020: collection suspended March 18 to May 9, 2020, and WT20 represents only the days covered; the weighting method changed each year from 2003 to 2006
2020 rows have WT06=0 (use WT20); some zero WT06 elsewhere per BLS practice
Weights sum to person-days, not persons: an average over days is not an average over people
Unweighted tabulations overstate activities done more often on weekends
BLS user's guide (June 2026 edition) and IPUMS RWT06 description read 2026-09-10

source: BLS ATUS user's guide (June 2026) (https://www.bls.gov/tus/atususersguide.pdf); IPUMS ATUS RWT06 (https://www.atusdata.org/atus-action/variables/RWT06)
